text:
maddy: @deploy-bot kicking off rollout for release v3.14 -> eu-west cluster. Change window 19:00-20:00 UTC. Canary set = 10% traffic (svc-a). Pin triggers: latency P95 > 200ms for 5m OR errors > 2% for 3m. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/escape-lane-runbooks#v3.14 :link:

alex: noted. canaries are on node-pool-eu-canary (labels: canary=true). Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/ops/deploys?orgId=1&var-release=v3.14

sam: quick Q — if we hit the latency pin, do we immediately pin to v3.13 or do we try a canary revert first?

maddy: good question. Two-step preference: 1) try canary-revert (pin subset to 3.13 for svc-a) to see if perf recovers within 10m. 2) if widespread, run full backout to v3.13 via deploy-bot. Both paths documented in runbook.

jose: adding concrete commands for ops (copyable):
```
# canary revert (10% traffic back to pinned version)
/deploy pin --service svc-a --version 3.13 --percent 10 --reason "canary revert due to latency"
# full backout
/deploy backout --release v3.14 --target-version 3.13 --force --reason "backout: latency trigger"
```

maddy: + escalate to oncall (sam) if backout occurs. escalation path in runbook: pager -> #eng-oncall -> exec oncall handoff. Also capture logs and attach to incident ticket.

deploy-bot: [system] scheduled rollout for v3.14 at 19:00 UTC. Canary: svc-a -> 10%. Rollout-id: 20260320-eu-041. Use /deploy status 20260320-eu-041 to follow.

runbook-bot: snippet from Escape Lane Runbook v2.1 (section 4 - fast backout):
1) Verify metric sources: grafana (latency), sentry (exceptions), rpm logs.
2) Run canary-revert command for svc-a. Wait 10m and observe P95.
3) If no recovery, escalate and execute full backout.
4) On backout, pin traffic and mark release as suspended in release ledger.
Link: https://confluence.redwood/escape-lane-runbooks/v2.1#fast-backout

alex: reminder: if KV cache mismatch suspected (we saw this on 3.10), run the cache-check script on canary hosts before full backout:
```
ssh ops@canary-01
sudo /opt/tools/cache-check --service svc-a --mode quick
```
If mismatched, follow cache invalidation steps (runbook sec 5).

sam: I'll be watching the dashboards at 19:00. If anything spikes, I'll trigger the canary revert and post the status here.

maddy: release notes summary for reviewers (paste):
- Feature: adaptive batching for embeddings (opt-in)
- Perf: kernel selector tuned for long context
- Fix: mem leak in async worker that could cause OOM at high QPS
Please put final release notes into the changelog after deploy.

jose: one more ops note — when executing /deploy backout, include the --artifacts-lock flag if we're reverting model weights to avoid partial roll-forward. Example:
```
/deploy backout --release v3.14 --target-version 3.13 --artifacts-lock
```

maddy: good call. Also tag the incident with `release:v3.14` and attach the canary traces.

alex: adding quick checklist to thread for whoever runs the backout:
- [ ] create incident ticket (ops template)
- [ ] run canary-revert (/deploy pin --percent 10)
- [ ] wait 10m, check P95/growth/5xx
- [ ] if no recovery -> /deploy backout (full) with --artifacts-lock
- [ ] pin traffic, update changelog and release ledger
- [ ] postmortem owner assigned

sam: copy. I'll be online and will post timestamps if I take action. :eyes:

maddy: thanks team. If anyone is off at 19:00, please @mention backup. Otherwise, deploy-bot will post status updates in this thread. :rocket:
